name: CircleCI
description: CircleCI is a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform that lets teams build, test, and deploy software automatically, with cloud, self-hosted runner, and on-premise Server deployment options.
best_for: Built for developers, platform engineers, and engineering managers at organizations of any size, from startups to enterprises, who need fast, reliable pipelines across mobile, AI/ML, and traditional software projects.
features: Configurable pipelines via YAML with parallelism and custom job workflows
Test splitting and intelligent test insights to speed up CI runs
Self-hosted runners for building on your own infrastructure
Automatic rollback pipelines for failed releases
Build caching and dependency caching to cut pipeline time
Integrations with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, AWS, GCP, and Azure

alternatives.name: Jenkins
alternatives.description: An open source automation server with a vast plugin ecosystem for building custom CI/CD pipelines.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want full control over a self-hosted, highly customizable CI/CD server.

alternatives.name: GitHub
alternatives.description: A developer platform for hosting code and automating workflows via GitHub Actions.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want CI/CD built directly into the same platform that hosts their code.

alternatives.name: GitLab
alternatives.description: An end-to-end DevSecOps platform spanning planning through deployment and security.
alternatives.best_for: Organizations wanting one consolidated platform for source control and CI/CD.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.unit: flat (includes 30,000 credits/month, up to 5 active users)
tiers.notes: No credit card required. Up to 6,000 build minutes/month on the small Docker resource class equivalent, 30x concurrency, 1GB network + 2GB storage included. Credits expire monthly and do not roll over.

tiers.name: Performance
tiers.unit: flat starting price, includes 30,000 credits + 5 active users
tiers.notes: Additional active users cost $15/user/month each. Additional credits cost $15 per 25,000-credit pack (~$0.0006/credit). 80x concurrency. Included monthly credits expire and do not roll over; separately purchased credit packs roll over and expire after 12 months.

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.notes: Unlimited concurrency, custom credit/user allotments, 50GB network + 200GB storage included, GPU/largest resource classes, enterprise controls, optional 24/7 support add-on. Requires contacting sales. Billing basis: annual (billed annually).

tiers.name: Server (self-hosted)
tiers.notes: Separate self-hosted deployment option shown under a 'Server' tab on the pricing page; no public numbers given. Billing basis: contact sales.

cons: The included monthly credit allotment (30,000 credits on both Free and Performance plans) expires at the end of each billing month and does not roll over -- unused capacity is simply lost every month, unlike separately purchased credit packs which roll over for 12 months (source: circleci.com/pricing/ and circleci.com/docs/guides/plans-pricing/credits/).

macOS/iOS builds carry a steep resource-class multiplier: CircleCI's own price list shows the macOS 'M4 Pro Medium' resource class costs 200 credits/minute versus 10 credits/minute for the Linux Docker Medium class -- a 20x cost multiplier for the same wall-clock build time, making mobile/macOS pipelines dramatically more expensive to run than equivalent Linux jobs (source: circleci.com/pricing/price-list/).

The Performance plan's per-seat surcharge stacks on top of usage-based credit billing: only 5 active users are included in the $15/month starting price, and every additional active user costs a flat $15/month regardless of how much compute they actually consume -- so a team's bill grows on two independent axes (seats and credits) rather than a single predictable metric (source: circleci.com/pricing/).
